missions.title: Raising Station
briefing: Fleet Command wants you on a higher station before the exercise begins. Raise your orbit from 80 km to a circular 120 km.
Burn PROGRADE to lift the far side of the orbit. Coast half an orbit to the new apoapsis, then burn PROGRADE again to bring the periapsis up to match.

lesson.concept: A burn changes the OPPOSITE side of your orbit
points: There is no brake pedal in orbit. Speeding up at one point raises the point on the far side of the planet; slowing down lowers it.
That is why raising a circular orbit takes two burns half an orbit apart: the first sets the new high point, the second lifts the low point to match.
Burn along PROGRADE (your direction of travel) to go higher, RETROGRADE to go lower.

coach.text: Lesson one, Commander. A burn changes the opposite side of the orbit. Burn prograde to raise the far side, then again at the top to circularize. I can fly it on your order.
On station. Remember: every burn takes effect half an orbit away.

missions.title: Rendezvous at Station
missions.summary: Close on the nav beacon 25 km ahead and match its speed.
briefing: A navigation beacon holds your orbit 25 km ahead. Close to within 300 m and hold relative speed under 2 m/s for 10 seconds.
Speeding up raises your orbit and slows you down. To catch a contact ahead, drop slightly lower, let it come to you, then burn TGT RETROGRADE to match speed.

objectives.label: Hold within 300 m of the beacon under 2 m/s

lesson.concept: Lower is faster: chasing means dropping down
points: Orbital speed falls as you climb. A lower orbit is shorter and quicker, so you drift ahead of anything higher and fall behind in a higher orbit.
To catch a target ahead of you, drop slightly lower, let the gap close, then climb back and match speed. Pushing straight at it only makes you higher and slower.
Relative speed is what matters. Match it before you arrive, or you will fly straight past.

coach.text: Beacon is ahead in our own orbit. Do not accelerate at it. Drop lower and we will overhaul it. The RENDEZVOUS order will fly the approach on request.
Still closing? Watch the range readout. Inside a few kilometres, start matching speed with target retrograde.

missions.title: Two-Beacon Patrol
missions.summary: Rendezvous with two beacons, one ahead and one astern.
briefing: Two navigation beacons share your orbit: one 25 km ahead, one 30 km astern. Rendezvous with the lead beacon first, then the tail beacon.

You have learned to overhaul a contact ahead by dropping lower. A contact astern is the mirror image: climb higher, slow down, and let it come to you. The skill is knowing which way to push, and when to stop.

lesson.concept: Phasing: pick your orbit to set the gap
points: The gap to another craft in the same orbit changes only because you are in a different one. Higher means longer and slower; lower means shorter and faster.
To go forward, descend. To go back, climb. Then return to the matching orbit when the gap is right.
Two beacons teach both directions. Use the pilot RENDEZVOUS order if a plan is troubling you.

coach.text: Two beacons. Lead beacon first, so we drop lower. Once matched, we climb and let the tail beacon overhaul us.
Lead beacon matched. Tail beacon is astern. We want a slower orbit now: retrograde to drop, then prograde to rise when it closes.

objectives.label: Match the lead beacon: within 300 m, under 2 m/s

missions.title: Live Fire
missions.summary: Weapons qualification: two target drones, missiles only.
briefing: Weapons are free. A target drone sits 15 km ahead in your orbit. Designate it with T and fire a missile with F.
A second drone will appear lower and astern once the first is down. Missiles hold a 400 m/s closing speed until their 800 m/s of delta-v is spent, so long shots are viable. You carry three.

objectives.label: Destroy Drone A with a missile
Destroy Drone B with a missile

lesson.concept: Missiles are spacecraft, with fuel of their own
points: A missile does not fly a straight line. It carries a fixed delta-v and spends it cancelling the sideways speed between it and the target, so a fast crossing shot costs far more than a slow one.
Shots from the same orbit are cheap because you and the target move together. Slow, matched shots are the efficient ones.
Lock a target with T and fire with F. The target and range show on your display.

coach.text: Weapons free. Designate the drone with T, then fire with F. It holds our orbit, so the missile will spend very little fuel closing.

missions.title: Crossing Traffic
missions.summary: Two drones on elliptical orbits will cross your lane. Stand by.
briefing: Two unarmed target drones are on elliptical orbits that cross your lane. They do not drift into range. They sweep through it, then swing away. Each pass lasts only minutes.
Use time warp to wait, but keep the range readout in view. When a drone closes inside about 30 km, designate it with T and fire. You have one missile per drone.

points: Two orbits that intersect put both craft at the crossing point only at certain moments. Miss that moment and the next one is a full orbit away.
Closing speed at a crossing can be high, and a missile spends delta-v cancelling it. Ready early and fire at the nearest approach.
Warp to save time, but drop out before they are inside 100 km.

coach.text: Drones are crossing our lane on ellipses. Nothing to chase. We hold at the crossing point and I will call them as they enter range.
First crossing is close. Designate the nearest drone and fire as soon as range allows.

missions.title: Long Reach
missions.summary: Target is beyond missile range. Close the distance first.
briefing: A target drone sits 130 km ahead in your orbit. A missile fired from here will run dry before it arrives, and you carry only two.
Close the distance first, then fire. Dropping to a lower orbit shortens the gap. The pilot's INTERCEPT order will fly it and stop at missile range.

lesson.concept: Weapon geometry: every shot has a reach
points: A missile is a small spaceship with a fixed delta-v. Its reach is a budget, not a speed. On a shared orbit that budget covers roughly 85 km.
Out of range, the missile coasts on and misses. The fix is to get closer, not to fire sooner.
Check the range readout, not the target marker.

coach.text: Target is outside our reach. Order an INTERCEPT, or drop lower yourself. Close to under 70 kilometres before firing.

objectives.label: Destroy the drone with a missile

missions.title: Operation Minefield
missions.summary: Seed the 88-91 km lane, then let the convoy find it.
briefing: A two-drone convoy, 1.5 km apart, will transit the 86.5 km lane. Climb into the 88-91 km corridor above it and lay three mines. A mine only counts if its whole orbit stays inside the corridor, so circularize before you drop.

Mines lie dormant until an enemy passes within 5 km, then pursue. A mine that closes to 2.2 km releases a kinetic vehicle, and that vehicle does the killing. Lower orbits are faster, so the convoy will overtake your field from astern and below.

objectives.label: Lay 3 mines with orbits inside 88-91 km
Let the mines destroy the convoy

lesson.concept: Mines are patient: orbit paths do the aiming
points: A mine drifts on its own orbit. If its orbit crosses a lane, anything passing by within 5 km wakes it.
A mine is only useful in the lane if its whole orbit stays in the lane. Circularize before you drop.
A lower, faster orbit overtakes everything above it. The convoy will catch your field from behind.

coach.text: Minefield laid. Now we wait. Use time warp, but keep clear of our own mines.

missions.title: Counter-Minelayer
missions.summary: Sink the enemy minelayer before you drift into its field.
briefing: An enemy minelayer is 40 km ahead and 4 km above you, seeding mines once you come within 20 km. Its mines go live inside 5 km.
Your lower orbit carries you forward beneath it. Three missile hits will break its hull. Fire early, or drop lower and pass beneath the field with room to spare.

lesson.concept: Your lower orbit is also a weapon: relative motion sets the clock
points: You are 4 km lower, so you move faster and pass beneath the minelayer. How fast you close decides how long your window is.
Hits take time to arrive. A missile that is already flying keeps working while you manoeuvre.
Targets dodge once a missile is close. Fire a second missile while the first is still in the air to make them choose.

coach.text: Minelayer is ahead and above. We close from below. Fire early, while it still has to dodge, and keep birds in the air.

missions.title: Under Fire
missions.summary: A gunboat engages from beyond your reach. Survive.
briefing: A gunboat 60 km ahead will fire missiles at you from outside your own range. You carry none. Survive six minutes after it opens fire.

A missile is only a threat while its fuel lasts. Every course correction costs it delta-v. Burn sideways early and often, then hold your course so it must spend more to catch you. Waiting until the last seconds is how ships are lost.

lesson.concept: Evasion: make them spend their fuel
points: A missile steers by burning. If you keep changing your path, it keeps burning, and its fuel runs out.
Burn across the line the missile is flying along (radial in or out), not toward or away from it.
The pilot's EVADE order does this automatically. Manual input cancels it.

coach.text: We are under fire at long range. With a missile in flight, burn radially. Early evasion costs it more than late. I can run EVADE on your order.

missions.title: Gunboat Duel
briefing: A gunboat holds station 35 km ahead, 3 km above your orbit. Its fire control locks inside 14 km and it carries two missiles. Two hits will sink you.
Your missiles face no such limit. It takes two hits and evades when a missile closes inside 5 km, so make every shot count. When it is down, a second gunboat will move in.

lesson.concept: Range wins duels: out-reach the enemy
points: The gunboat can only lock on within 14 km. Your missiles reach much farther.
A target dodges by burning sideways. A single missile gives it plenty of time; two missiles in flight overwhelm it.
If you cannot win the range fight, break contact and burn away. Distance is safety.

coach.text: Enemy lock range is 14 kilometres. Stay outside it and fire from range. If we must close, close from below, where we are faster.

missions.title: Convoy Escort
missions.summary: A raider hunts the freighter, not you. Stop it.
briefing: A freighter shares your orbit, 4 km ahead. A raider is coming up from below and astern, and its missiles are aimed at the freighter. You are not its target, but you are the only escort.

The raider closes from a lower, faster orbit. It will pass beneath you before it reaches the freighter, and that is your window. Missiles take time to arrive and it evades, so fire early and fire twice.

lesson.concept: Multi-craft combat: protect a ship, not yourself
points: The enemy flies toward its target, not toward you. That predictable path is yours to intercept.
Fire from the side where your orbit gives the longest window. A shot taken early arrives before the raider is near the freighter.
Losing the freighter loses the mission, whatever your own health.

coach.text: Raider is coming up from astern and below. It wants the freighter. Designate it as soon as it enters missile range and keep birds in the air.

missions.title: Task Force
missions.summary: Lead a flight: a wingman against a gunboat and a minelayer. Focus fire.
briefing: You lead a two-ship flight. Your wingman, a gunboat, is 6 km ahead and will engage whatever the enemy sends at it. The enemy has a gunboat 40 km astern of you and a minelayer 40 km ahead.
You cannot fight everything at once. Divide the enemy. Sink the gunboat first, because it can kill you, while the minelayer only seeds the lane. Then turn on the minelayer. Stay out of its field.

points: Count threats, then kill the one that can hurt you first. Anything that can only drop mines can wait.
A wingman is a force multiplier: it draws fire and adds missiles. Keep it alive.
Two missiles from two ships arrive together and a target can only dodge one.

coach.text: Two threats. The gunboat astern can sink us. The minelayer only seeds. Gunboat first.
Gunboat down. Minelayer next. Stay out of its minefield and let the wingman support.

missions.title: Kestrel
missions.summary: A gunboat that finally fights back with its thrusters.
briefing: Intelligence has the gunboat Kestrel 50 km ahead on a matching orbit. She has a pilot now. When a bird closes she lights her engines once and slides sideways.
One missile will not do it, because she has time to get clear. Put two birds in the air together so that she can only dodge one.

lesson.concept: Saturation: more than one threat at once
points: A reactive pilot answers one threat with one burn. A second missile arrives while she is still turning.
Fire both birds within a few seconds of each other.
Spares matter: keep a missile in reserve in case the first pair misses.

coach.text: Kestrel is a reactive pilot. She dodges one bird, not two. Fire both together.

missions.title: Shrike
missions.summary: Shrike sees a bird coming and starts running early.
briefing: Shrike is a gunboat with a patient pilot. She watches your missiles from the moment they leave the rail, burns early, and keeps burning until the bird has nothing left to chase her with.
Engines run hot. Watch her heat: a ship that has burned for a long time cannot burn hard. Make her spend it, then finish her.

lesson.concept: Attrition: make the dodger spend her heat
points: Dodging costs heat, and heat caps thrust.
A missile that is dodged is not wasted if it drains the target's cooling margin. Keep birds flying.
Fire in waves, not all at once, and shoot when she is sluggish.

coach.text: Shrike dodges early and for long. Spend her heat with a steady stream of birds, then close.

missions.title: Hunter
missions.summary: The adversary comes after you, and her gun has a longer reach than yours.
briefing: Hunter is a gunboat that flies at you. She closes to her standoff range, puts her nose on you and fires two missiles when she is inside her lock range. She also dodges.
You cannot sit and wait. Fire as she comes in, then keep moving. Her missiles are as lethal as yours.

lesson.concept: Pursuit: the enemy closes to engage
points: A pursuer trades her heat for position. When she is hot, she cannot dodge.
Open fire at long range while she closes; every second she spends burning towards you is a second she is not dodging.
Burn away if she gets inside her lock range.

coach.text: Hunter is closing on us and carries two birds. Hit her while she is still hot from the approach.

missions.title: Wolf Pack
missions.summary: Two adversaries, one flight plan. Do not let them set the range.
briefing: Two gunboats, Fang and Talon, hold your orbit 50 km ahead and 40 km astern. Fang dodges early; Talon pursues.
Kill Talon first because she will close with you. Then run Fang down.

points: Kill the pursuer first. The dodger is no threat to you.
Two ships can bracket you; do not stay between them.
Burn away from the second ship while you work the first.

coach.text: Two adversaries. Talon pursues from astern. Fang dodges ahead. Talon first.

missions.title: Last Convoy
missions.summary: A raider that can think about your freighter and about you. Keep the freighter alive.
briefing: A freighter shares your orbit 4 km ahead. Reaper, an expert raider, is closing from below and astern. She goes for the freighter, dodges your birds well and punishes anything that gets inside her lock.
You have eight birds and no margin for waste. Fire in waves and keep her spending heat on dodges while the freighter slips away.

lesson.concept: Everything together: protect, pursue and out-heat
points: Protect the freighter first, yourself second.
Every dodge Reaper makes costs her heat; stack threats until she cannot afford another.
Use your orbit: a lower pass gives you speed and a shorter window.

coach.text: Reaper is the best pilot we have met. Keep birds in the air and keep the freighter alive.
